questions.question: Which of the following describes a luminous object?
options: An object that gives out its own light
An object that only reflects light from other sources
An object that allows light to pass directly through it
An object that absorbs all light that falls on it

questions.question: When light enters the human eye, through which part does it enter, and where is it detected?
options: Enters through the retina and is detected by the pupil
Enters through the pupil and is detected by the retina
Enters through the iris and is detected by the lens
Enters through the lens and is detected by the cornea

questions.question: What is an echo, and how is it produced?
options: An echo is when sound is absorbed completely by a soft surface.
An echo is when a sound is heard again after reflecting off a hard surface and travelling back.
An echo is when sound waves bend around a corner in an empty room.
An echo is when sound travels faster through a solid than through air.

questions.question: Why do soft surfaces absorb a large amount of sound?
options: Because they reflect sound waves in many regular directions.
Because sound waves transfer energy by making the particles in the soft surface vibrate.
Because soft materials contain no particles, creating a small vacuum.
Because the strong forces between their particles prevent any movement.

questions.question: In a reflection diagram, what is the 'normal'?
options: A line drawn parallel to the mirror's surface
An imaginary line drawn at 90° to the point of reflection
The path that the incoming light ray takes
The angle between the mirror and the reflected ray

questions.question: If a ray of light hits a flat mirror with an angle of incidence of 35° to the normal, what is the angle of reflection?
options: 35° on the same side of the normal
55° on the other side of the normal
35° on the other side of the normal
90° to the mirror surface

questions.question: If you stand 2 metres in front of a flat mirror, how far behind the mirror does your reflection appear to be?
options: 1 metre
2 metres
4 metres
It appears right on the surface of the mirror

questions.question: When you look at your reflection in a plain mirror, how does the image appear?
options: Upside down and laterally inverted
Right way up and not inverted at all
Right way up but laterally inverted
Upside down and not inverted

questions.question: What is the primary difference between transparent and opaque objects?
options: Transparent objects transmit light through them, whereas opaque objects do not.
Transparent objects reflect all light, whereas opaque objects absorb all light.
Transparent objects scatter light, whereas opaque objects let it pass cleanly.
Transparent objects emit their own light, whereas opaque objects do not.

questions.question: How is a shadow formed?
options: By a transparent object letting light pass through to a single point.
When an opaque object blocks light, leaving an unlit area in its shape.
When light waves bend around a soft object and cancel each other out.
By regular reflection of light off a highly polished surface.

questions.question: How does the amplitude of a vibration affect the sound produced?
options: A greater amplitude results in a higher pitch sound.
A greater amplitude results in a louder sound.
A smaller amplitude results in a louder sound.
Amplitude only affects the speed of the sound, not how loud it is.

questions.question: What is frequency, and how does it relate to the pitch of a sound?
options: It is a measure of vibration size; a higher frequency produces a louder sound.
It is a measure of how often vibrations occur; a greater frequency produces a higher pitch.
It is a measure of sound speed; a lower frequency produces a faster sound.
It is the distance a sound wave travels; a lower frequency produces a lower volume.

questions.question: Why does sound travel faster through liquids than through gases?
options: The particles in liquids are closer together, so vibrations are passed on more easily.
Liquid particles are held by much stronger forces than solids.
Gases absorb all vibration energy, preventing sound from travelling.
Liquids are much warmer than gases on average, speeding up the sound waves.

questions.question: Through which state of matter does sound travel the fastest, and why?
options: Gases, because the particles are far apart and can move freely without hitting each other.
Solids, because strong attractive forces between particles mean many vibrate when one does.
Liquids, because the particles can slide past each other easily to carry the sound.
A vacuum, because there are no particles to block the path of the sound wave.

questions.question: Why is it impossible for sound to travel through a vacuum?
options: Because a vacuum is too cold for sound waves to exist.
Because there are no particles in a vacuum to vibrate and pass on the sound wave.
Because light travels too fast in a vacuum and blocks the sound.
Because the gravitational forces in a vacuum pull the sound waves downwards.
